sampling distribution: the probability distribution of a sample statistic (p-hat or X-bar) over all possible random samples of size n; in this module's picture, the pile. See [The pile of p-hat](#/math3042-q9/phat-sampling-distribution).
sample proportion|p-hat: $\hat{p} = X/n$, the share of successes in one sample; one blue dot on the pile. See [The pile of p-hat](#/math3042-q9/phat-sampling-distribution).
population proportion: $p$, the true share of the whole population that has the property; the pink line, which is never seen in real life. See [The pile of p-hat](#/math3042-q9/phat-sampling-distribution).
standard error|standard error of the mea: the standard deviation of a sampling distribution, that is, the width of the pile: $\sqrt{pq/n}$ for p-hat, $\sigma/\sqrt{n}$ for X-bar. See [The pile of X-bar](#/math3042-q9/xbar-sampling-distribution).
margin of error: $E = z_{\alpha/2}\sqrt{pq/n}$, the distance from the centre of the pile that holds the stated share of all samples (95% for 1.96). See [The margin of error](#/math3042-q9/margin-of-error).
critical value|critical Z: $z_{\alpha/2}$, the Z value with area $\alpha/2$ to its right: 1.645 for 90%, 1.96 for 95%, 2.576 for 99%. See [The margin of error](#/math3042-q9/margin-of-error).
confidence interval: the range $\hat{p} - E$ to $\hat{p} + E$, built from one sample, that covers the true p for the stated share of samples. See [A confidence interval for p](#/math3042-q9/ci-for-p).
confidence level: $1 - \alpha$, the share of samples whose interval covers the truth: typically 0.95. See [90%, 95%, 99%](#/math3042-q9/ci-confidence-level).
Central Limit Theorem|CLT: the sample mean X-bar is approximately normal when X itself is normal or when the sample size is 30 or more, with mean $\mu$ and standard deviation $\sigma/\sqrt{n}$. See [When the pile is a bell](#/math3042-q9/clt-shape-rule).
QQ plot|quantile-quantile plot: sorted sample values plotted against the Z-scores a perfect normal sample of the same size would have; a straight line means the data are consistent with a normal population. See [The QQ plot](#/math3042-q9/qq-plot).
qqnorm: the R function that draws a QQ plot of a vector against the normal distribution. See [The QQ plot](#/math3042-q9/qq-plot).
qqline: the R function that adds the reference line to a QQ plot, through the first and third quartiles. See [The QQ plot](#/math3042-q9/qq-plot).
replicate: the R function that runs an expression m times and returns the m results as a vector; used to make many sample means. See [Simulate X-bar in R](#/math3042-q9/r-simulate-xbar).
two-way table: a table of counts with one variable down the rows and another across the columns; `table(a, b)` in R. See [Load a CSV and count two columns](#/math3042-q9/r-load-two-way-table).
